derived: GSK turned 18.02% of revenue into free cash over 2023 to 2025 against the 19.3% its filed expense lines leave. Checked before interest: interest paid is booked under financing, so free cash flow is already struck before interest, so the charge stands. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 1.44% to 0.00%. Restated without one-off cash: GSK's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried 1,867mm GBP of legal settlements. None recurs, so the charge stays nil. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 21.54% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 23.77%, so the charge rebuilds at -2.23%. It was held at nil, but GSK books 808mm GBP of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside its cost lines in FY2025 (0001131399-26-000004), 2.47% of revenue, so the charge takes the rebuilt figure: -2.23%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 GSK's cash flow statement shows receivables up 1,109mm GBP, inventories up 858mm GBP, payables down 63mm GBP, a working capital build of 2,030mm GBP, 2.15% of revenue. column11: a judgement, and the competitive case is this. Nintedanib is approved for chronic fibrosing ILD with a progressive phenotype and is the incumbent the trial's population is already failing or tolerating badly; tocilizumab is approved in SSc-ILD but not here; mycophenolate and rituximab are used off label. Belimumab would be the first B-cell-pathway agent with a label in this population, and it arrives as an add-on to standard therapy rather than a replacement, which widens use but caps share. Set against that, belimumab's own penetration in its approved disease is modest: 5,831 Part D plus 3,685 Part B Medicare beneficiaries in 2024 against a CDC-registry US lupus prevalence of 204,295
